**Step 1 — Scene:** A cooked breakfast: fried eggs, grilled tomatoes and mushrooms. Toast is on a separate plate, so it is excluded; the yogurt and drink are also outside the target plate.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A round plate, approximately **24 cm** in diameter. Area = 3.14 × 12² = **452 cm²**.

**Step 3 — Items:** Two fried eggs, two grilled tomato halves, several cooked mushrooms, and a small amount of visible cooking fat.

**Steps 4–7 — Area, volume, weight and energy:**

| Item | Plate area | Area × average height = volume | Density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Two eggs | 36% | 163 cm² × 0.65 cm = 106 ml | 1.0 | 106 g | 145 | 154 kcal |
| Tomato halves | 23% | 104 cm² × 1.5 cm = 156 ml | 0.7 | 109 g | 22 | 24 kcal |
| Mushrooms | 7% | 32 cm² × 1.4 cm = 45 ml | 0.65 | 29 g | 28 | 8 kcal |
| Cooking fat | Thin surface sheen, overlapping food | Approximately 3 ml | 0.92 | 3 g | 884 | 27 kcal |

The food footprints total **66% of the plate**. Cooking fat overlaps these footprints rather than covering additional plate area. Fat is counted separately from the eggs and vegetables.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **247 g and 213 kcal** is plausible for two eggs, two tomato halves and a small portion of mushrooms, with only a light amount of cooking fat. The largest uncertainty is the amount of fat.
